newsitem.title: BOLIVIA: SOCCER SHOWCASE-WORLD'S TOP STRIKER, KEEPER CLASH IN COPA.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER SHOWCASE-WORLD'S TOP STRIKER, KEEPER CLASH IN COPA.

text.p: Brazil meet their smaller neighbours Paraguay on Sunday in a clash that pits one of the world's top strikers against the man who claims to be the world's best goalkeeper.

Brazil forward Ronaldo and Paraguay's unorthodox and volatile goalkeeper Jose Luis Chilavert are the top attractions in a fascinating Copa America quarter-final between the world champions and South America's in-form team.
Paraguay lead the single South American World Cup qualifying group and their shock defeat against Ecuador in the first round of the Copa America last week was their first for 13 months.
But the two teams do not meet in the qualifiers as Brazil advance automatically into next year's World Cup in France as champions.

At first point, Paraguay look to be out of their depth. Brazil, with a population nearly 40 times that of Paraguay, are four-times world champions and the only team to have played in every tournament.
Paraguay, coached by Brazilian Paulo Cesar Carpegianni, have never gone beyond the last 16 in their three appearances in the tournament.

The contrasts between the two sides are huge. Brazil, many of whose players are multi-millionaires, attract hordes of admirers where ever they go and their every move is followed by a corps of around 400 reporters.
Humility is the catchword in the Paraguay camp, where Chilavert is the only player who enjoys the trappings of stardom.

Local rivalries and Paraguay's well-known fighting spirit, however, mean that Brazil rarely get an easy game and at South American level, the gulf narrows significantly. Brazil have won the Copa America four times, all at home, and Paraguay twice.
The two teams have been thrown together after Brazil won their first round group, with a 100 percent record, while Paraguay went through as the one of the best third-placed teams.
Brazil's Ronaldo-Romario attack, described this week as "almost unstoppable" by former Argentina coach Carlos Bilardo, will be up against one of South America's meanest defences.
Carlos Gamarra, the foundation of the Paraguayan backline, plays for Brazilian club Internacional and is considered one of the best defenders in Brazilian football.
Right-back Francisco Arce is another who knows the Brazilians well, having played for Brazilian champions Gremio for the last three years.
A set-piece expert, he is likely to have his hands full trying to stop the surging runs of Brazil's left-back Roberto Carlos and attacking midfielder Denilson.
Chilavert is also one of his team's most attacking options, thanks to his amazing ability at free kicks and penalties.
He is currently top scorer for Argentina's Velez Sarsfield, where he plays his club football, and will be champing at the bit for a chance to score against the Brazilians.

In the 1-1 draw with Argentina on Tuesday, he scored one goal from a penalty, appeared to intimidate Argentina's Marcelo Gallardo when he fired a penalty high and wide, and was involved in the incident that led to the sending-off of Argentina's Pablo Rotchen.
His huge goal kicks up field frequently reach the opposition's penalty area and could be a real problem for Brazil's defence.

Brazil coach Mario Zagallo has chopped and changed his central pairing recently, although the Goncalves-Aldair partnership he used in Thursday's 2-0 win over Colombia looked the best of the ones he has tried.
The stronger defence, however, was only achieved by adopting ultra-defensive tactics, which angered the Brazilian fans in the crowd.
Afterwards, Zagallo said: "I would rather play ugly football and win than play attractive football and lose.
"You can play well one day, more or less the next day and badly another day, but the important thing is the victory," Zagallo said.
